events.summary: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger released the 2026 Virginia Energy Plan (about 200 pages plus a 22-page brief). One scenario uses 'noncombustion natural gas resources such as fuel cells' as a near-term bridge. Market coverage (tier 3) reports the plan creates a 'non-combustion gas resource' category and allows up to 5 GW of it from 2029 to 2035; the 5 GW figure was NOT confirmed against the plan document itself. Bloom is not named in the plan per Cardinal News.
events.why_it_matters: Virginia has the world's biggest data center cluster; a state plan that explicitly makes room for fuel cells widens the potential market for Bloom's product, though it is a planning document, not an order.

sources.name: Virginia Energy, 2026 Virginia Energy Plan (PDF, not opened)

events.summary: CEO KR Sridhar on Bloomberg TV played down Oracle's force majeure notice on Project Jupiter (up to 2.45 GW of Bloom capacity), saying Bloom units are 'fungible': 'after we ship the units, after they're on the trucks, we can redirect the trucks to go to some other location'.
events.why_it_matters: Management's answer to the biggest open risk (a delay at its largest project): if a site slips, boxes can go to another customer. That is a claim, not proof; revenue timing could still shift.

events.summary: Barclays (Christine Cho) kept Equal-Weight and raised its price target to $308 from $276, citing a newly acquired second Fremont, California factory (158,000 sq ft vs the existing 164,000 sq ft) that could lift capacity to 10-12 GW from 5-6 GW, and Ameren Missouri's resource plan including 500 MW of natural gas fuel cells by 2030. RBC (Christopher Dendrinos) reiterated Outperform, $335 target. Morgan Stanley Overweight, $310 (reported).
events.why_it_matters: Opinions, not facts. They contain one factual input worth noting: a utility (Ameren) planning fuel cells as grid supply, which would be a new type of buyer for Bloom.

events.summary: BE closed +4.17% at $289.15 (intraday high $297.59). Onsite-power and hydrogen names rallied as a group: FuelCell Energy +7%, Global X Hydrogen ETF (HYDR) +3%, S&P 500 about +0.7-1.0%. Pipeline attribution: market part +1.65%, industry part +4.23%, company-specific -1.71% (z -0.39), i.e. mostly explained by market and industry.
events.why_it_matters: Friday's gain was not Bloom-specific news; it moved with its group. This stock has a 1-year beta of about 4.2 vs the market, so it swings far more than the index.

events.summary: Chief Commercial Officer Aman Joshi sold 8,437 shares at $277.17 on 2026-10-01 (about $2.34M), under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-11-26; he still owns 147,092 shares (sale was about 5.4% of his holding). The shares came from RSUs that vested Aug-Sep 2026. Prior planned sales: 3,601 shares on 2026-09-16 and 4,677 on 2026-08-14. Directors Jeffrey Immelt (81 sh) and Cynthia Warner (83 sh) received routine stock grants on 2026-09-30.
events.why_it_matters: Pre-scheduled sale of newly vested pay stock; says little about management's view. Not a thesis breaker.

events.summary: Oracle sent a force majeure notice on Project Jupiter, the roughly $165B AI data center campus in Dona Ana County, New Mexico, built by Blue Owl's STACK Infrastructure for OpenAI and expected to use up to 2.45 GW of Bloom fuel cells. A natural-gas pipeline for the site slipped to February 2027 after permitting setbacks. Oracle said Jupiter 'remains on our planned schedule'; Blue Owl said the notice 'does not change the financial commitments'; Bloom said Oracle 'remains committed to Project Jupiter and to its contract with Bloom Energy'. BE then rose 8% to $288.77 on 2026-09-25.
events.why_it_matters: Jupiter is the single largest project in Bloom's pipeline. A force majeure notice lets Oracle defer certain payments if the campus is late; a delay would push Bloom revenue later even if the contract survives. This is the closest thing to a thesis-breaker candidate (order delay) and must be watched.

events.summary: Q2 2026: revenue $1,065.4M (+165.5% y/y from $401.2M), product revenue $935.4M (+215.4%), service revenue $69.0M, GAAP gross margin 33.4% (non-GAAP 34.3%), operating income $182.2M (vs a $3.5M loss), operating cash flow $226.4M, GAAP EPS $0.62, non-GAAP EPS $0.78 (reported consensus about $0.39, tier 3). Full-year 2026 guidance raised to revenue $3.9-4.2B, non-GAAP gross margin about 34%, non-GAAP operating income $800-900M, non-GAAP EPS $2.55-2.85. Company says all major US hyperscalers and over a dozen neoclouds, AI labs and colocation operators have approved its systems.
events.why_it_matters: This is the fundamental reason the stock has more than tripled this year: sales are growing very fast AND it has turned profitable with positive cash flow, which addresses both points of Santi's proposed thesis.

events.summary: Hunterbrook Media reported that Bloom relies on Chinese scandium (a rare metal used in its fuel cells), tracing 'four separate China-linked routes' into its supply chain, and questioned its financials. BE fell 5.7% to $254.29 that day. Bloom called the claims 'false and misleading' and said its scandium supply is not dependent on China. A securities class action was filed 2026-07-30 in the Northern District of California (class period 2025-02-27 to 2026-07-08); lead-plaintiff deadline was 2026-09-28.
events.why_it_matters: An open supply-chain and legal risk: if China-linked supply were restricted, production could be affected; the lawsuit is pending. No regulator action found.

events.summary: S&P Dow Jones announced on 2026-09-04 that Bloom would join the S&P 500; inclusion took effect before the open on 2026-09-21. Separately, on 2026-04-13 Bloom and Oracle expanded their master agreement to up to 2.8 GW of fuel cells, with an initial 1.2 GW contracted and deploying (Oracle also holds a warrant issued 2026-04-09).
events.why_it_matters: Index inclusion forces index funds to own the stock and signals it is now a large company (market cap about $85B reported). The Oracle agreement is the largest disclosed customer framework.

products.name: Bloom Energy Server (solid-oxide fuel cell power system)
products.what_it_is: A refrigerator-sized box that turns natural gas (or hydrogen) into electricity on site through a chemical reaction instead of burning it.
products.analogy: Like a battery that never runs down as long as you keep feeding it gas: no flame, no turbine, just a chemical reaction that pushes out electricity.
products.buyers: AI data center owners and operators (Oracle, Brookfield's AI factories, colocation operators, neoclouds), utilities (AEP and, per Barclays, Ameren Missouri in its plan), factories, hospitals and other commercial and industrial customers.
products.how_it_works: Stacks of ceramic cells (using scandium-containing materials) run hot; natural gas is converted to hydrogen-rich gas and reacts electrochemically with oxygen from the air, producing electricity and heat. Units are modular: add more boxes to add megawatts, and they can be installed in weeks to months versus years for a grid connection.
products.sales: Unit or MW shipments not found in the Q2 release. Proxy (labelled): Q2 2026 product revenue $935.4M, total revenue $1,065.4M; FY2026 revenue guidance $3.9-4.2B. Oracle master agreement up to 2.8 GW with 1.2 GW initially contracted. Backlog figure not disclosed in the Q2 release (Barclays says backlog growth outstrips revenue growth: opinion).
products.stage: Shipping and ramping in volume; second Fremont factory acquired (reported 2026-09-29 via City of Fremont post and analyst notes, not a company release found) to expand capacity.
products.size_for_company: Core business: product revenue was about 88% of Q2 2026 revenue ($935.4M of $1,065.4M).
products.competition: Gas turbines and reciprocating engines (e.g. GE Vernova, Caterpillar, Siemens Energy), other fuel cells (FuelCell Energy), batteries plus grid power, and future small nuclear reactors. Bloom's pitch is speed of installation and lower local emissions (no combustion).
products.why_investors_care: It is the product behind the AI-power story; fast growth plus first real profits drove the stock up about 233% year to date.
products.watch_next: Q3 results (late October): product revenue, MW shipped if disclosed, backlog, any update on Project Jupiter timing, factory capacity plan.
